summary: Header parsing, the metadata table, the row and size estimates, the pass order and the specs all check out. The headline Falisse finding is wrong in its main inference. Exactly one 4-male/4-female subset of the 11 AddBiomechanics subjects (subject_0, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 9, 10) reproduces every cohort statistic the TBME 2017 paper reports, at the paper's rounding: age 29.8 +/- 3.9 y, height 176 +/- 6.6 cm, mass 69.6 +/- 6.0 kg. So the folder very likely contains the paper's 8 volunteers plus 3 additional men (subject_1, 7, 8). The 'ages outside 29.8 +/- 3.9 contradict the cohort' argument, which also appears on the review sheet, treats a standard-deviation band as a range. What genuinely stays unresolved is the 3 extra people and the trials: the files hold Gait/STS/StairUp, while the paper reports other motions. Smaller fixes: the mass-ratio minimum is 0.71 (subject_9 0.706), not 0.72; and option A's 'fetchable by hash' needs qualifying, because the B3D is deleted after conversion.

Paper: KU Leuven manuscript (lirias 494460; fetched, sha256 prefix d53f6559, equal to the worker's), section II.A: 'Eight healthy volunteers (four males and four females, age 29.8 +/- 3.9 years, height 176 +/- 6.6 cm, and weight 69.6 +/- 6.0 kg)'.
AddBiomechanics headers: 11 distinct records, 7 male and 4 female, ages 24-43. Confirmed.

Subset test (my code): of the 35 possible 4M/4F subsets of the 11, exactly one reproduces all six reported values when rounded as the paper rounds. It is subject_3, 0, 10, 2, 4, 5, 6, 9: age 29.8/3.9, height 176.0/6.6, mass 69.6/6.0. The 3 left over are men (subject_1 43 y, subject_7 37 y, subject_8 39 y).
A chance match of six statistics in one of 35 subsets is very unlikely. The folder is most plausibly the paper's cohort plus 3 additional men.

The audit's consequence ('Eleven distinct people cannot be eight volunteers' eleven legs, and ages up to 43 sit far outside 29.8 +/- 3.9') and the HIST-04 sheet caption ('Dots outside the grey band ... contradict the paper's cohort') misuse a mean +/- SD band as a range. They do not establish a mismatch for the 8.

What does remain unmatched: the 3 extra subjects, and the trials. The B3D trials are Gait/STS/StairUp, while the paper reports six motions including squat, stair descent and squat jump (audit quote). So protocol facts and the task mapping still cannot be taken from the paper without confirmation.
